beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “An agent that drives a Chromium browser via Screenshot, FindElement, Click, and Type.” Read the summary; scroll no further.

verify.note: OPERATOR: README.md:12 and :15 are stale against 0.4.0 — `crewhaus run crewhaus.yaml` with no --prompt dies on a TTY (browser run is single-turn), and there is no BROWSER_HEADLESS knob (chromium is always headless). Keep the preview on the summary paragraph; this driver demos the bundle, not those lines.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the planner and the grounding model are both Anthropic.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and which runtime spine to compile.”

beats.label: Add the agent + planner model
beats.cue: One model does the planning — which tool to call next, and where.

beats.label: Write the tool contract
beats.cue: “Be deliberate: ONE screenshot, find the target, click its center, ONE more to verify.”

beats.label: Add the driver block
beats.cue: Chromium, a 1024×720 viewport, and a startUrl — loopback, which the driver blocks on purpose. Beat 3 shows why.

beats.label: Name the grounding model
beats.cue: FindElement's eye — it turns “the green Submit button” into center coordinates.

beats.label: Open the permissions block
beats.cue: mode: default — every tool has to be allowed by name, or it stops and asks.

beats.label: Allow the six tools by name
beats.cue: Six alwaysAllow rules — one per tool the instructions name. Anything else stops and asks.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: Parse, then the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target browser (driver + groundingModel + permission rules)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it to its gate: GREEN.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (10 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the initial --prompt gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: One file. The instructions, the model, the viewport, the startUrl — constants at the top. No YAML at runtime.

beats.label: Show what the bundle imports
beats.cue: Screenshot, mouse+keyboard, vision grounding: real packages, not prompt text. Note the first one.

verify.note: 5 tool imports — navigate, screen-capture, mouse-keyboard, vision-grounding, catalog

beats.label: Show the permission rules
beats.cue: The six alwaysAllow rules, compiled in — and Navigate, which the bundle just imported, is not one of them.

verify.note: one match (the emitted RuleSet) + 9 lines: flag/settings and the six yaml alwaysAllow rules — Navigate absent, so mode default resolves it to "ask"

beats.label: Add Playwright to the bundle
beats.cue: Playwright is an optional peer dep — you install it only when you want chromium.

verify.note: @crewhaus/computer-use-driver declares playwright as an OPTIONAL peer dep, so the bundle install never pulls it

beats.label: Show which chromium it pins
beats.cue: Exactly which build, and where it lands — before you spend the bandwidth.

verify.note: prints Chrome for Testing + Chrome Headless Shell + ffmpeg: version, install location, download URL. Downloads nothing.

beats.label: Fetch the chromium build
beats.cue: [manual] One-time: that exact chromium, into the shared cache.

verify.note: ~150MB browser-binary download; run it once before the take — the verifier never runs it (the --dry-run beat above proves the invocation form)

beats.label: Launch the bundle
beats.cue: [needs-key] No --prompt and a TTY: one live browser context, turn after turn.

verify.note: 0.4.0 runs chromium HEADLESS with no knob to change it (createDriver hardcodes headless: true), so the browser window is never on camera — the JSON event stream and the model's answers are the take

beats.label: Look at the start page
beats.cue: [needs-key] The startUrl is loopback, and 0.4.0 routes chromium through a DNS-pinning proxy that blocks private targets. The screenshot shows the guard, not a page.
beats.text: Take ONE screenshot and tell me, in one sentence, exactly what this page says.

verify.note: the proxy answers 127.0.0.1:7325 with a 403 text body (`ssrf-pinning-proxy: blocked target IP 127.0.0.1`); the bundle still emits {"kind":"navigated"} because page.goto() resolves on a non-2xx

beats.label: Ask it to go somewhere real
beats.cue: [needs-key] Navigate was never in the six rules — so mode: default stops the turn and asks.
beats.text: Navigate to https://crewhaus.ai and take ONE screenshot.

verify.note: the REPL prints `approve Navigate {"url":"https://crewhaus.ai"} [y/N] > ` — do NOT tap the next beat until that prompt is on screen, or the next line answers it as "no"

beats.label: Grant it, once
beats.cue: [needs-key] One keystroke, one call. Screenshot, FindElement and Scroll never ask — they're in the six.

verify.note: answers the approval prompt; the grant is not remembered — a second Navigate asks again

beats.label: Ground an element
beats.cue: [needs-key] FindElement returns a bounding box and a center — coordinates, from pixels.
beats.text: Use FindElement to locate the primary call-to-action button and give me its center coordinates.

beats.label: Act on the page
beats.cue: [needs-key] Scroll is destructive; the alwaysAllow rule is why it never stops to ask.
beats.text: Scroll down one screen, take ONE more screenshot, and tell me what changed.

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell; the browser context closes with it.

groups.title: One more thing · scripted, not interactive

beats.label: Run one turn, non-interactively
beats.cue: [needs-key] browser_start, navigated, browser_done — JSON events on stdout. The CI shape.
beats.command: bun live/dist/agent.ts --prompt "Take ONE screenshot and tell me, in one sentence, exactly what this page says."

verify.note: one prompt, one turn, then exit — no REPL. Screenshot is in the six rules, so nothing has to ask.

beats.label: Or pipe the prompt in
beats.cue: [needs-key] No --prompt, no TTY: the bundle reads the task off stdin — and with nothing to ask, Navigate is denied outright.
beats.command: echo "Navigate to https://crewhaus.ai and take ONE screenshot." | bun live/dist/agent.ts

verify.note: two things at once: the bundle falls back to readStdin() when --prompt is absent and stdin is not a TTY; and a single-turn surface cannot prompt, so the runtime collapses Navigate's "ask" to a denial whose tool_result names the fix (`{ type: alwaysAllow, pattern: Navigate }`). It lands in the browser_done finalText, not as a crash — exit 0.
